title_en: Interpretation of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Article 13, Paragraph 1 and Article 19 of the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: I. With respect to question (1) submitted for interpretation by the Court of Final Appeal of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. In accordance with Article 89, paragraph (9) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of China, the State Council, i.e., the Central People's Government, shall exercise the power to administer foreign affairs of the State. State immunity rules or policies fall within the category of diplomatic affairs in the State's foreign affairs, and the Central People's Government shall have the power to determine the state immunity rules or policies of the People's Republic of China, which shall be uniformly implemented within the territory of the People's Republic of China. Based on the foregoing, and in accordance with the provision of Article 13, paragraph 1 of the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China that "the Central People's Government shall be responsible for the foreign affairs relating to the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region," the administration of foreign affairs relating to the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region falls within the power of the Central People's Government, and the Central People's Government shall have the power to determine the state immunity rules or policies applicable in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

II. With respect to question (2) submitted for interpretation by the Court of Final Appeal of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. In accordance with Article 13, paragraph 1 of the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China and Article 1 of this Interpretation, the Central People's Government shall have the power to determine the state immunity rules or policies applicable in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region; in accordance with Article 19 of the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China and Article 3 of this Interpretation, the courts of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall have no jurisdiction over the acts of the Central People's Government in determining the state immunity rules or policies. Therefore, when the courts of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region encounter issues concerning jurisdictional immunity and enforcement immunity of foreign states and their property in hearing cases, they must apply and implement the state immunity rules or policies determined by the Central People's Government to be applicable to the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. Based on the foregoing, and in accordance with the provisions of Article 13, paragraph 1 and Article 19 of the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China, the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, including its courts, shall have the duty to apply or implement the state immunity rules or policies adopted by the Central People's Government, shall not deviate from the aforesaid rules or policies, and shall not adopt any rules different from the aforesaid rules or policies.

III. With respect to question (3) submitted for interpretation by the Court of Final Appeal of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. State immunity concerns whether a court of a state has jurisdiction over a foreign state and its property, and whether a foreign state and its property enjoy immunity in the court of a state, which directly relates to the foreign relations and international rights and obligations of that state. Therefore, determining state immunity rules or policies constitutes an act of state involving foreign affairs. Based on the foregoing, "acts of state such as defense and foreign affairs" as provided in Article 19, paragraph 3 of the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China shall include the act of the Central People's Government in determining state immunity rules or policies.

IV. With respect to question (4) submitted for interpretation by the Court of Final Appeal of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. In accordance with Articles 8 and 160 of the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China, the laws previously in force in Hong Kong shall be maintained only to the extent that they do not contravene the Basic Law. Pursuant to Article 4 of the Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on the Handling of the Laws Previously in Force in Hong Kong in accordance with Article 160 of the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China, the laws previously in force in Hong Kong that have been adopted as the laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall, from 1 July 1997, be applied with such modifications, adaptations, limitations or exceptions as are necessary to bring them into conformity with the status of Hong Kong after the resumption of the exercise of sovereignty by the People's Republic of China and with the relevant provisions of the Basic Law. As a local administrative region of the People's Republic of China that enjoys a high degree of autonomy and is directly under the Central People's Government, the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region must implement the state immunity rules or policies determined by the Central People's Government. The rules on state immunity in the laws previously in force in Hong Kong must comply with the above provisions in order to continue to apply after 1 July 1997. Based on the foregoing, and in accordance with Article 13, paragraph 1 and Article 19 of the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China, the rules on state immunity in the laws previously in force in Hong Kong that have been adopted as the laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region pursuant to the Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on the Handling of the Laws Previously in Force in Hong Kong in accordance with Article 160 of the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China shall, from 1 July 1997, be applied with such modifications, adaptations, limitations or exceptions as are necessary to conform with the state immunity rules or policies adopted by the Central People's Government.
This is hereby announced.
